summary_en: Can workers in low-wage regions move into high-paying jobs without leaving their region? Elekes uses Swedish administrative micro-data to track individual workers across jobs over time and finds that local access to skill-related, high-wage occupations — i.e., to industries that draw on overlapping skills — substantially raises the probability of escaping low-wage employment. Pure regional growth helps less than the *composition* of the local labour market: a related-variety upgrade is the key mover.
data_used: Swedish population-level administrative microdata linking individuals' annual employment, occupation, wage, and residence over a multi-year window. Skill-relatedness between occupations measured from labour-flow patterns; analysis of low-to-high-wage transitions at the worker level.
policy_relevance: Concrete input to Hungarian regional and labour-market policy: rather than chasing every kind of inward investment, planners should value FDI and re-skilling programmes that build *related* industries on top of an existing local skill base. For ITM industrial-strategy and EFRE smart-specialisation Hungary should map county-level skill-relatedness and prioritise sectors that are skill-adjacent to current local employment, not greenfield sectors with no skill bridge.
title: Regional diversification and labour market upgrading: local access to skill-related high-income jobs helps workers escaping low-wage employment
journal: Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society
